text:
I am an undergraduate student majoring in mathematics and applied mathematics. I am currently an exchange student at the University of California, Berkeley. My home university is Xiamen University Malaysia.
I am generally interested in High-Dimensional Statistics, Stochastic Processes, PDEs, and Computational Topology, combining computational methods with empirical analysis.

title: Boting Zhang(张柏霆)
text:
Current Projects
Here are the research projects I am currently working on at the University of California, Berkeley:

GRiD Project: Statistical Modeling for Multimodal Learning Analytics — ERDL Lab, UC Berkeley

Supervised by Ratih Ayu Apsari
Multivariate Time-Series & Spectral Modeling: Formulates parametrized eye-tracking recordings as regularized multivariate time series, applying autoregressive (AR/VAR) modeling, spectral analysis, and time-frequency decomposition to capture multi-scale dynamics in fixation rates and gaze kinematics.
Hierarchical Spatial & Markov Transition Dynamics: Characterizes gaze trajectories across hierarchical Areas of Interest (AOIs) via 1-second and embedded jump-chain Markov processes, higher-order \(n\)-step motif significance testing, and stationary-baseline overlap tests to separate coordinated multi-participant joint visual attention from coincidental co-occurrence.
Time-Aligned Linguistic & Behavioral Encoding: Uses natural language processing (NLP) and behavioral annotation to encode verbal explanations, discourse transitions, and non-verbal cues into synchronized temporal feature sequences.
Cross-Modal Synchronization & Cognitive Shift Detection: Evaluates spectral coherence and dynamic coupling across gaze kinematics, spatial transitions, and linguistic streams to uncover measurable signatures of cognitive shifts during mathematical and embodied reasoning tasks.

Estimation Method Project: Diagnostic Classification Models (DCMs) — D-Lab, UC Berkeley

Supervised by Jonathon A. Pedroza (JP)
Conjunctive & Disjunctive Model Formulation: Formulates and compares DINA (AND-rule) and DINO (OR-rule) diagnostic classification models across a \(2^K\) latent attribute space induced by a prespecified \(Q\)-matrix, contrasting unrestricted item-specific slipping and guessing parameters against restricted common-error variants (rDINA and rDINO).
Comparative Estimation & Bayesian Inference: Expresses marginalized item responses as a finite-mixture likelihood and benchmarks Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation, and full Bayesian posterior inference via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC).
Prior Specification as Statistical Regularization: Evaluates uniform versus weakly informative Beta priors on item-error parameters, framing prior specification as a formal regularization device to mitigate boundary solutions and improve numerical stability in sparse latent-class models.
Latent-Class Recovery & Predictive Diagnostics: Assesses parameter recovery, posterior uncertainty, and predictive adequacy on a five-attribute probability-and-statistics assessment using posterior predictive replications, item-level discrepancy checks, and root mean squared error (RMSE).
